characteristics.cultivar: Camellia sinensis var. assamica, ancient arbor trees (gu shu), aged 100–300+ years

description.short: The most prestigious and coveted sheng pu-erh terroir — powerful, thick, with pronounced energy ("cha qi") and lasting sweetness
description.overview: The Bulang ethnic village of Lao Banzhang is revered as the undisputed "King" of pu-erh terroirs — its tea is famous for extraordinary power and thickness, coupled with bitterness that swiftly yields to overwhelming sweetness.
description.leaf: Large, thick dark-green leaves from ancient forest tea gardens
description.liquor: Ranging from bright golden-yellow to deep luminous amber depending on age
description.aroma: Potent, floral-honeyed, with deep forest undertones
description.taste: Extremely thick and full-bodied, with an initial bold bitterness that rapidly transforms into intense sweetness (hui gan) — the hallmark of this terroir
description.aftertaste: Exceptionally long finish accompanied by pronounced "cha qi" (warmth, energetic invigoration, and light perspiration)
description.processing: Hand-plucking from old trees → withering → pan fixation at lower temperature → rolling → sun-drying (maocha) → steam compression into cakes → natural aging

history.origin: Lao Banzhang is a village of the indigenous Bulang people on Bulang Mountain; historically remote and rugged, it remained outside mainstream tea trade routes for centuries
history.development: Fame and elite status arrived in the 2000s when collectors and traders recognized the unmatched strength and density of tea from its old arbor trees
history.modern: Today Lao Banzhang is one of the most expensive and frequently counterfeited pu-erh terroirs in the world; certified old-tree harvest commands prices far above surrounding villages
interestingFacts: Due to astronomical market demand, Lao Banzhang is widely considered one of the most counterfeited tea terroirs in China
The local village committee established strict checkpoint controls and harvest tracking seals to combat fraudulent tea and protect the village's reputation
